legacy_delta: Skills extension does not exist in 2025-11-25 or 2025-06-18 schemas/spec at all (grep of schema.ts, 2026-07-28_schema.json, and the 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 schemas for 'skill' returns nothing) — it is new as of / introduced under revision 2026-07-28 and lives entirely outside the core schema.ts, defined only by the separate ext-skills repository referenced from pages/extensions__skills__overview.md.

The extension builds on primitives (Resources, pagination, caching, resultType envelope) that are part of the core 2026-07-28 spec; an SDK targeting only 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 cannot support Skills at all since resultType/caching/pagination-for-resources semantics it depends on are current-revision features.

methods.name: skills/list
methods.capability_gate: Server MUST declare capabilities.resources (object, possibly empty) AND capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/skills"] (object; may be {} or {directoryRead:true}). Client MUST only send skills/list after observing this declaration.
methods.params: Supports pagination: optional params.cursor (string) per standard MCP pagination utility. No other params documented in the page (example shows params: {}).
methods.result: { resultType: "complete" (REQUIRED literal per this extension), skills: SkillEntry[], ttlMs: number (REQUIRED), cacheScope: string e.g. "public" (REQUIRED), nextCursor?: string for pagination }. SkillEntry = { uri: string (resource URI of SKILL.md, e.g. skill://code-review/SKILL.md), frontmatter: object (ALL YAML frontmatter fields verbatim, at minimum name and description), resources: Array<{uri:string, digest:string ("sha256:<hex>"), size:number}> | the literal string "dynamic" for generated/unstable content }.
methods.notes: Manifest (resources array) MUST include SKILL.md itself plus every supporting file. Each returned entry is complete/self-sufficient (client need not call skills/get afterward). Servers MAY return empty or partial listings (i.e., listing completeness is not guaranteed) but per-skill entries, once listed, must have complete manifests (manifest MUST NOT be split across pages).

methods.name: skills/get
methods.capability_gate: Same capability gate as skills/list (resources + io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension declared).
methods.params: { uri: string } — REQUIRED. The URI may originate from a user, another skill, or server instructions (i.e., need not come from a prior skills/list call).
methods.result: { resultType: "complete", skill: SkillEntry (same shape as a skills/list entry), ttlMs: number, cacheScope: string }.
methods.notes: Servers MUST respond to skills/get for every skill they serve, INCLUDING skills that do not appear in any listing (hosts MUST support loading by URI even for unlisted skills). Also usable to refresh/re-verify an existing retained entry. Unknown URI -> JSON-RPC error -32602 (Invalid params); this is the documented lookup-failure path that stops skill loading.

methods.name: resources/read
methods.capability_gate: Base Resources capability (capabilities.resources); this is the pre-existing core Resources primitive, reused (not redefined) by the Skills extension to fetch SKILL.md and supporting file bytes.
methods.params: { uri: string } (standard resources/read params — page does not add extension-specific params).
methods.result: Standard resources/read result shape: { resultType: "complete", contents: [{ uri, mimeType, text (or blob) }], ttlMs, cacheScope }. Example: SKILL.md returned with mimeType "text/markdown" and text containing YAML frontmatter + body.
methods.notes: Reading SKILL.md via resources/read does NOT itself activate the skill — activation requires the host to route the read through its own skill-loading path (verification + optional user approval) before the content enters model context. Relative references inside a skill (e.g. references/checklist.md) resolve against the skill's root directory using the skill:// (or server-chosen) scheme, and are fetched from the SAME originating server via another resources/read call. Hosts MUST NOT prefetch any file (including SKILL.md itself) ahead of actual need — not on connection, not on listing, not on approval; approval binds to the manifest, not to fetched bytes.

methods.name: resources/directory/read
methods.capability_gate: Optional method. Client MUST NOT call it unless the server's extension declaration sets directoryRead: true (default is false when the extension object is present but omits the key).
methods.params: { uri: string (a directory URI, no trailing slash) ; cursor?: string for pagination }.
methods.result: { resultType: "complete", resources: Array<{ uri: string, name: string, mimeType: string }>, nextCursor?: string }. Child directories are reported with mimeType: "inode/directory" (exact constant). Returns direct children only (non-recursive); client descends by issuing another request per child directory.
methods.notes: For skills with a static manifest, hosts MAY answer directory queries purely from that retained manifest instead of calling the server. Hosts MUST NOT treat a live directory/read result as extending/augmenting the retained manifest, and MUST NOT expose newly-observed files as part of the skill without an entry refresh (skills/get) plus any required re-approval.

requirements.text: Servers that support Skills MUST declare both the resources capability and the io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension object in server/discover.
Servers that declare the io.modelcontextprotocol/skills extension MUST implement skills/list and skills/get.
Skill files SHOULD be served through the existing resources/read method rather than a new method (stated as the design; skills/get returns metadata only, not content).
Clients MUST issue skills/list and skills/get only after observing the server's extension declaration.
Every request (including skills/list and skills/get) MUST include the required request metadata (_meta) per basic/index#_meta, even though examples omit it for brevity.
A manifest (the `resources` field of a skill entry) MUST include SKILL.md and every supporting file, each with uri, SHA-256 digest, and byte size.
List and get results MUST include resultType: "complete", ttlMs, and cacheScope.

Hosts MUST preserve both server identity and skill URI together (skill identity = server identity + URI) in registries, approvals, and caches, because names are only labels and are not guaranteed unique.
Servers SHOULD use the skill:// URI scheme.
Servers MAY use a scheme other than skill://.
Hosts MUST NOT identify a resource as a skill solely by its URI scheme.
Servers MAY return empty or partial listings from skills/list.
Servers MUST respond to skills/get for every skill they serve, even ones absent from any listing.
Hosts MUST support loading a skill by URI, including skills that do not appear in a listing.
A SKILL.md file MUST begin with YAML frontmatter containing name and description.
The final path segment of the skill's parent directory MUST match the frontmatter's name field.
Hosts MUST NOT retrieve (fetch) skill files ahead of actual need — not on connection, not on listing, not on approval. Approval binds to the manifest without requiring file retrieval.
Clients MUST NOT call resources/directory/read unless the server declares directoryRead: true.
For skills with a manifest, hosts MAY answer directory queries from the retained manifest instead of the server.
Hosts MUST NOT treat a live directory/read result as extending the retained manifest, or expose newly listed files as part of the skill, without a refreshed entry and any required re-approval.
An unknown/unlisted URI passed to skills/get returns JSON-RPC error -32602 (Invalid params) and loading stops.
If lookup fails, approval is denied, or verification fails, the host MUST NOT load or use the content.
While acting on a skill, the host MUST retain the entry used to load it, at least until SKILL.md leaves model context.

For skills with a manifest, hosts MUST: (1) restrict file reads to URIs present in the retained manifest; (2) verify each file's raw byte size and SHA-256 digest before use; (3) parse SKILL.md frontmatter and compare it field-by-field with the entry's stored frontmatter.
Hosts MUST NOT use content that fails verification (digest, size, or frontmatter mismatch).
Persisted approval MUST bind to the complete set of file URIs and digests; any changed/added/removed file revokes that approval and the host MUST re-obtain approval before loading or executing.
Hosts SHOULD cache verified content on demand.
Disk caches MUST either (a) prevent modification of cached files by the model/tools/other users and keep them immutable, or (b) verify cached bytes on every access.
Hosts MUST exclude cached skill files from filesystem-skill discovery paths and MUST preserve their MCP origin across restarts.
Hosts MAY decline skills whose resources are declared "dynamic" (no stable digests).
For dynamic ("resources":"dynamic") skills that are accepted, hosts MUST still verify frontmatter and MUST NOT treat persisted approval as covering arbitrary future content.
Servers MUST serve valid Agent Skills and implement the declared methods, including base Resources support.
Servers MUST preserve all frontmatter fields and publish complete manifests computed from the actually-served bytes, unless declared "dynamic".
Servers MUST support direct lookup (skills/get) independently of listing; each skill entry is atomic and its manifest MUST NOT be split across pages.
Servers declaring directoryRead: true MUST support every directory in the served skill namespaces.
Servers SHOULD NOT exceed 512 files or 16 MiB per skill, including SKILL.md.
Hosts MUST support skills up to the 512-files/16-MiB limits.
Hosts MAY support larger skills than the 512-file/16-MiB guideline.
Security: hosts MUST prevent skills with the same name from silently replacing one another.

Security: hosts MUST tag loaded content with its originating server and bind resource reads to that server via a host-assigned label; cross-server reads require explicit per-call approval naming both servers.
Security: hosts MUST treat skill content as untrusted input; host-side code execution and permission grants such as allowed-tools require explicit per-skill user approval.
Security: hosts MUST obtain fresh user consent before activating a nested skill; reading its SKILL.md merely as supporting content does not activate it or apply its frontmatter.
Unknown skill/file or invalid directory URI -> JSON-RPC error code -32602 (Invalid params).
Internal server failure while serving skills -> JSON-RPC error code -32603 (Internal error).

wire_details: Extension capability key (exact string): "io.modelcontextprotocol/skills", nested under top-level capabilities.extensions in the server/discover response.
Extension capability object shape: {} (bare, support without directory reading) or { "directoryRead": boolean } (optional field, default false).
Methods (exact JSON-RPC method strings): "skills/list", "skills/get", plus reuse of core "resources/read" and optional "resources/directory/read".

skills/list result fields: resultType (must be literal "complete"), skills (array), ttlMs (number, e.g. 300000), cacheScope (string, e.g. "public"), nextCursor (optional, standard pagination cursor field).
SkillEntry fields: uri (string), frontmatter (object, arbitrary YAML-derived fields incl. required name/description), resources (array of {uri, digest, size} OR the literal string "dynamic").
skills/get params: { uri }. skills/get result: { resultType: "complete", skill: SkillEntry, ttlMs, cacheScope }.
resources/read result for a skill file: { resultType: "complete", contents: [{ uri, mimeType, text }], ttlMs, cacheScope }; mimeType example "text/markdown".
resources/directory/read params: { uri } (directory URI, no trailing slash), optional cursor. Result: { resultType: "complete", resources: [{ uri, name, mimeType }], nextCursor? }.
Directory entries for child directories use mimeType constant: "inode/directory".

URI scheme convention: "skill://<skill-name>/<path>", e.g. "skill://code-review/SKILL.md", "skill://code-review/references/checklist.md"; scheme is a SHOULD convention, not mandatory, and MUST NOT be used by hosts as sole proof of skill-ness.

Error codes used: -32602 (Invalid params) for unknown skill/file or invalid directory URI/lookup failure; -32603 (Internal error) for internal server failure. These are the standard JSON-RPC reserved codes, not new Skills-specific codes.
SKILL.md frontmatter is YAML, delimited by --- ... --- at file start; required keys: name, description. Body is markdown after the frontmatter block.
Size/scale limits: SHOULD NOT exceed 512 files or 16 MiB per skill (including SKILL.md itself); these are soft server-side limits paired with a MUST for hosts to support up to them.

No dedicated skills/read or skills/activate method exists — content retrieval is exclusively via resources/read; there is no separate wire method for 'activation' (activation is a host-local, non-protocol concept).
sdk_implications: PowerShell SDK server-side: to support Skills, a server implementation must (a) declare capabilities.resources and capabilities.extensions."io.modelcontextprotocol/skills" (with directoryRead flag) at server/discover time, (b) implement skills/list and skills/get handlers returning the exact SkillEntry shape with resultType/ttlMs/cacheScope, (c) implement/extend resources/read to serve SKILL.md and supporting files by URI with correct mimeType, (d) optionally implement resources/directory/read only if directoryRead:true is declared, honoring no-trailing-slash directory URIs, inode/directory mimeType for subdirs, and cursor/nextCursor pagination.

SDK server helper should compute and cache SHA-256 digests + byte sizes of skill files at publish/registration time (a build-time or load-time manifest generator), since manifests MUST be computed from actually-served bytes and MUST NOT split across pagination.

SDK should validate at registration time: SKILL.md starts with YAML frontmatter containing name+description, and the final path segment of the skill's directory matches frontmatter.name — reject/error otherwise, since this is a server MUST.
SDK server should support a 'dynamic' skills mode: allow a skill provider to return resources: "dynamic" instead of a computed manifest for generated content lacking stable digests.

SDK client-side: implement typed calls for skills/list (with cursor pagination) and skills/get (by uri), a resources/read wrapper scoped to skill URIs, and an optional resources/directory/read call gated on the server's declared directoryRead capability (client MUST refuse to call it otherwise).

SDK client must implement a 'retained entry' / manifest cache keyed by (server identity, skill URI) — not skill name alone — supporting: file-read restriction to manifest URIs, per-file SHA-256+size verification before handing content to callers, frontmatter re-comparison against the stored entry, and invalidation-on-mismatch with a re-fetch-via-skills/get path.

SDK client should expose hooks/callbacks for host-level policy decisions the spec explicitly delegates: user-approval gating (initial load, manifest change, nested skill activation, cross-server reads, allowed-tools grants), since these are host MUST requirements the generic client library cannot decide on its own — but the SDK must provide the extension points and refuse to proceed without an approval decision when the policy requires one.
SDK client should NOT prefetch skill file contents eagerly on connect/list/approve — lazy, on-demand resources/read only, per host MUST NOT prefetch requirement.

SDK should implement optional disk-cache utilities satisfying the immutable-or-reverify-on-access requirement, and must tag any cached file with its originating server id so it can be excluded from local filesystem-skill discovery and reattributed correctly after restart.

Error handling: SDK must surface -32602 as a typed 'unknown skill / invalid uri' error distinct from -32603 'internal error', and must NOT treat digest/size/frontmatter verification failures as protocol errors — these are host-side logic (throw/return a distinct SDK-level VerificationError, not a JSON-RPC error object).

Because Skills is an extension (not core schema.ts), the SDK's type definitions for SkillEntry, manifest resource entries, and capability declaration must live in an extension-specific module (mirroring how other io.modelcontextprotocol/* extensions are structured), not in the core Requests/Results union — schema.ts and 2026-07-28_schema.json contain zero references to 'skill', confirming this must be hand-modeled from the ext-skills spec text, not generated from the core schema.
open_questions: The page references 'the full specification' at github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-skills/blob/main/specification/stable/skills.mdx for complete security/approval/origin/cache rules; that repo is not available locally and github.com HTML is blocked for curl in this environment, so finer-grained normative details (e.g., exact JSON schema types for frontmatter validation, any additional error conditions, exact allowed-tools grant format) beyond what's quoted on the overview page could not be verified against the canonical source.
Whether skills/list and skills/get support any request params beyond cursor/uri (e.g., filtering, search) is not specified on this page — the example shows empty params for skills/list.

Whether there is a server-to-client notification for skill manifest changes (push-based invalidation) versus purely client-initiated refresh via skills/get is not addressed; the spec only describes client-driven refresh.

The exact structure of 'allowed-tools' permission grants mentioned in Security Considerations is not defined in this file — referenced only by name, full shape presumably lives in the external ext-skills repo (Agent Skills specification at agentskills.io).

No mention of a capability version number or extension schema version field beyond the capability object itself — unclear whether the extension key co-exists with a semantic version for forward compatibility.
Client matrix link (/extensions/client-matrix) for concrete SDK/client conformance status was not fetched; not available locally.

summary: Skills is an MCP extension (capability key "io.modelcontextprotocol/skills") letting servers expose Agent-Skills-format workflows (a directory with SKILL.md + optional files) for discovery/retrieval via existing Resources primitives. Servers supporting it MUST declare both capabilities.resources and the extension object (optionally {directoryRead:true}) at server/discover, and MUST implement two new methods: skills/list (paginated, returns SkillEntry[] with uri, frontmatter, and a resources manifest of {uri,digest,size} or "dynamic") and skills/get (by uri, returns a single complete SkillEntry, works even for unlisted skills). Actual file bytes are fetched via the pre-existing resources/read (SKILL.md, supporting files) and optionally resources/directory/read (gated by directoryRead, non-recursive, "inode/directory" mimeType for subdirs). All three response types MUST carry resultType:"complete", ttlMs, cacheScope. Skill identity = (server identity, uri), not name. SKILL.md MUST have YAML frontmatter with name+description, and its directory's final path segment MUST equal name. Hosts bear heavy verification/security duties: never prefetch, restrict reads to the retained manifest, verify SHA-256 digest+size+frontmatter before use, treat manifest changes as approval-revoking, treat skill content as untrusted, gate code-execution/allowed-tools/nested-skill-activation/cross-server-reads behind explicit user approval, and exclude skills from silent name collisions. Error model reuses plain JSON-RPC -32602 (unknown skill/file/bad directory URI) and -32603 (internal error); verification failures are host-side, not protocol errors. Soft size limit: servers SHOULD NOT exceed 512 files/16MiB per skill; hosts MUST support up to that. Entirely absent from schema.ts/2025 schemas — new, extension-only, not part of core protocol types.</summary>
